In a current-carrying loop placed in a magnetic field, when is the torque maximum?

options.text: When the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the field
When the plane of the loop is parallel to the field

text_solutions: The torque on a current-carrying loop in a magnetic field is given by \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \). It is maximum when \( \sin \theta = 1 \), i.e., \( \theta = 90^\circ \), meaning the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

qns_content.text: Why is the magnetic field outside a long solenoid considered negligible?

text_solutions: In a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines are concentrated inside, and outside, the fields from opposite sides of the coils cancel each other, making the external field nearly zero.

qns_content.text: A square loop of side \( 0.18 \, \text{m} \) with 30 turns carries \( 2 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 60^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?
What is the effect on the magnetic force if a charged particle’s velocity is doubled while keeping the magnetic field constant?

text_solutions: The magnetic force \( F = q v B \sin \theta \) is directly proportional to velocity \( v \). Doubling the velocity doubles the force.

qns_content.text: An electron moves at \( 4.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.35 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force? (Charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

Why does a charged particle describe a circular path when moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field?

options.text: Due to the magnetic force acting as centripetal force

text_solutions: The magnetic force \( \mathbf{F} = q (\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}) \) acts perpendicular to the velocity, providing the centripetal force needed for circular motion when the velocity is perpendicular to the field.

qns_content.text: A long straight wire carries a current of \( 18 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at a distance of \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) from it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))

What is the SI unit of magnetic field strength?

text_solutions: The SI unit of magnetic field strength is the tesla (T), defined as the field producing a force of 1 N on a 1 C charge moving at 1 m/s perpendicular to the field.

text_solutions:
\( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with normal.

\( \tau = 12 \times 3.5 \times 0.07 \times 0.5 \times \sin 60^\circ = 1.47 \times 0.866 = 1.273 \approx 1.27 \, \text{N m} \).

\( \tau = 25 \times 3 \times 0.04 \times 1.2 \times 1 = 3.6 \, \text{N m} \).

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the shunt resistance in converting a galvanometer to an ammeter?

text_solutions: A shunt resistance is connected in parallel with the galvanometer to allow most of the current to bypass it, reducing the effective resistance and enabling the measurement of larger currents.

What is the nature of the force between two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions?

text_solutions: Two parallel wires with currents in opposite directions experience a repulsive force because the magnetic field produced by one wire interacts with the current in the other, causing them to push apart.

What is the direction of the magnetic force on a positive charge moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field?

text_solutions: The magnetic force is given by \( \mathbf{F} = q (\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}) \). \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 0^\circ = 1 \) with normal.

\( \tau = 10 \times 5 \times 0.07 \times 0.8 \times 1 = 2.8 \, \text{N m} \).

options.text: Plane of the loop is parallel to the field

text_solutions: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \) is zero when \( \sin \theta = 0 \), i.e., \( \theta = 0^\circ \) or \( 180^\circ \), meaning the plane of the loop is parallel to the magnetic field.

text_solutions:
\( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to the plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with the normal.

\( \tau = 10 \times 3 \times 0.02 \times 0.5 \times \sin 60^\circ = 0.3 \times 0.866 = 0.2598 \approx 0.26 \, \text{N m} \).

What happens to the torque on a rectangular current loop if the magnetic field direction is reversed?

text_solutions: Torque is given by \( \boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{m} \times \mathbf{B} \). Reversing the magnetic field \( \mathbf{B} \) reverses the direction of the torque vector, but its magnitude remains the same.

Which factor does not affect the magnetic field produced by a current element according to the Biot-Savart law?

text_solutions: The Biot-Savart law states \( d\mathbf{B} \propto \frac{I d\mathbf{l} \times \mathbf{r}}{r^3} \). The field depends on current, length of the element, distance, and angle, but not on the mass of the conductor.

text_solutions: Magnetic field lines form closed loops because there are no magnetic monopoles, unlike electric field lines, which originate from positive charges and terminate at negative charges or extend to infinity.
